chapter_title: Measurement and Interpretation of Rock Properties

sections.title: Intact Rock Properties
sections.summary: Intact rock properties measured by: (1) uniaxial compressive strength qu (ASTM D7012): peak axial stress at failure; E50 from slope of stress-strain curve at 50% of qu; (2) Brazilian tensile strength (ASTM D3967): σt = 2P/(πDl); (3) direct shear on rock joints (ASTM D5607): peak and residual friction angle φj with optional JRC roughness quantification; (4) point load index Is (ASTM D5731): qu ≈ 22 × Is(50) (correction to 50 mm diameter); (5) Schmidt hammer rebound R → qu and E50 per Table 9-3 and 9-4. Sample selection: avoid weathered, fractured, or mechanically damaged specimens; sufficient L/D ratio (≥ 2.0 for UCS).
sections.body:
Intact rock strength and stiffness: The uniaxial compressive strength qu (or UCS) is the axial stress at failure in an unconfined compression test. E50 = Young's modulus at 50% of qu from the axial stress-strain curve. Poisson's ratio from simultaneous lateral strain measurements. Tests on intact specimens; values must be adjusted for in situ rock mass quality using classification systems.

Brazilian tensile strength (ASTM D3967): Indirect tensile test on disk-shaped specimen; σt = 2P/(πDl) where P = load, D = diameter, l = thickness. Useful when direct tensile strength is needed.

Direct shear on rock joints (ASTM D5607): Peak and residual friction angles for natural or manufactured discontinuities. Joint roughness coefficient (JRC) from Barton and Choubey (1977) quantifies surface texture; smooth = 0, very rough = 20. JRC combined with JCS (joint compressive strength) and φr (residual friction angle) gives strength envelope.

Point load index (ASTM D5731): Quick field test on drill core or irregular rock lumps; Is = P/De² where De = equivalent diameter. Normalize to 50 mm: Is(50). Empirical: qu ≈ 22 × Is(50) for irregular lumps; correlation varies by rock type.

Schmidt hammer: R value → qu and E50 from Table 9-3 (Deere and Miller 1966) and Table 9-4. Simple portable tool for preliminary assessment. Large scatter in correlations; should not replace direct UCS testing for design.
key_points: UCS (ASTM D7012): qu = peak axial stress; E50 from stress-strain at 50% qu; L/D ≥ 2.0
Brazilian tensile: σt = 2P/(πDl) — indirect; use when direct tensile needed
Point load index: qu ≈ 22 × Is(50); quick field test but significant scatter
Schmidt hammer R → qu and E50 (Tables 9-3, 9-4); preliminary screening only
JRC (0–20) + JCS + φr: Barton-Choubey discontinuity shear strength parameters

sections.title: Rock Mass Classification and Deformability
sections.summary: Rock mass classification systems: RMR (Rock Mass Rating, ASTM D5878/Bieniawski 1989) — sums 5 parameters: UCS, RQD, discontinuity spacing, discontinuity condition, groundwater; range 0–100 (0 = very poor, 100 = excellent). GSI (Geological Strength Index, Hoek et al. 2013) — from rock mass structure and discontinuity surface condition charts; quantitative version from Jcond89 and RQD. Rock mass modulus Em from Hoek and Diederichs (2006): Em = Ei × [0.02 + (1-D/2)/(1+e^((60+15D-GSI)/11))]; D = disturbance factor (0 = undisturbed, 1 = heavily blasted). Hoek-Brown failure criterion for rock masses: σ1 = σ3 + qu × (mb×σ3/qu + s)^a; mb, s, a from GSI and mi (Table 9-10).
sections.body:
Discontinuity characterization: Strike and dip describe planar orientation; plotted on stereonets for stability analysis. Downhole televiewer (acoustic or optical) provides high-resolution images of borehole wall for discontinuity characterization without core orientation tools.

RMR system (ASTM D5878, Bieniawski 1989): Five parameter rating system (Table 9-5): (1) UCS of intact rock; (2) RQD; (3) Spacing of discontinuities; (4) Condition of discontinuities (roughness, opening, infill, weathering, length); (5) Groundwater conditions. Sum of 5 ratings (0–100): 81–100 = Class I Very Good; 61–80 = Class II Good; 41–60 = Class III Fair; 21–40 = Class IV Poor; 0–20 = Class V Very Poor. Correction for joint orientation applied for specific applications.

GSI (Geological Strength Index, Hoek et al.): Reflects rock mass structure (blockiness) and surface condition of discontinuities. Estimated from chart (Figure 9-23) or quantitative chart (Figure 9-24) using Jcond89 (Table 9-7) and RQD.

Rock mass modulus: Em from Hoek and Diederichs (2006): Em = Ei × [0.02 + (1-D/2) / (1 + e^((60+15D-GSI)/11))] where Ei = intact rock modulus, D = disturbance factor. Table 9-9 provides guidance on D. Also from plate load tests, pressure meter (Chapter 8 methods), and seismic velocity.

Hoek-Brown failure criterion: σ1 = σ3 + qu × (mb × σ3/qu + s)^a where mb = mi × exp((GSI-100)/(28-14D)); s and a depend on GSI (Equations 9.31, 9.32). Represents curved failure envelope for interlocked rock masses; can be converted to approximate Mohr-Coulomb c' and φ' for given stress range.
key_points: RMR (ASTM D5878): 5 parameters; sum 0-100; Class I (81-100) excellent to Class V (0-20) very poor
GSI: rock mass structure + discontinuity surface condition; quantified from Jcond89 and RQD
Hoek-Diederichs rock mass modulus: Em = Ei × [0.02 + (1-D/2)/(1+e^((60+15D-GSI)/11))]
Disturbance factor D: 0 = undisturbed in situ; 1 = heavily blasted — reduces Em significantly
Hoek-Brown: σ1 = σ3 + qu(mb×σ3/qu + s)^a; mb, s, a from GSI and mi (Table 9-10)
